projects.name: TripFlow
projects.text: Corporate travel API built around three production problems: concurrent approvals competing for one budget, booking retries, and failures between the database and the broker.
projects.stack: PHP 8.3 · Laravel 12 · MySQL · Redis · RabbitMQ · Docker · Pest · Larastan
bullets: SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the cost center keeps two approvals from spending the same balance; a two-connection MySQL test proves the second one waits for the lock.
An Idempotency-Key replays the saved response, a Redis lock serializes booking and cancellation, and a transactional outbox publishes to RabbitMQ only after commit.

projects.name: Nexora Core
projects.text: Digital wallet with deposits, transfers, refunds, disputes that hold the amount, and statements.
projects.stack: PHP 8.4 · Laravel 13 · MySQL 8.4 · Docker · PHPUnit · Larastan level 8
bullets: Money in cents and an immutable ledger: a reversal is always a new operation. MySQL triggers and grants keep the application itself from changing balances or entries, and a scheduled reconciliation checks every balance.
Wallets locked in a fixed order and an idempotency key per form; concurrency tests with separate PHP processes. Cursor pagination took a 1-million-entry statement from up to 2.2 s to under 100 ms.

projects.name: GEMP
projects.text: Credit comparison tool that queries three providers in parallel and ranks offers by total cost, showing what can still be delivered when a provider is slow or down.
projects.stack: Go · net/http · WebAssembly · React · TypeScript · GitHub Actions
bullets: Each provider runs in a goroutine with context.Context and a 250 ms deadline; partial results when one fails and 503 when none answer. The demo runs the same Go code compiled to WebAssembly, tested in CI.
